problem.title: Card-fraud scoring service
problem.context: A payments company scores every card transaction for fraud before it is authorized. It processes about 3,000 transactions per second on a normal day and up to five times as many during seasonal sales. Fraudsters adapt within weeks, and the confirmed fraud labels (chargebacks) arrive days to weeks after the transaction. Auditors and the card schemes can ask, months later, why a given transaction was scored the way it was. The ML team has five data scientists and two ML engineers. The company's operations team runs the data centres and the shared infrastructure, but there is no platform team for machine learning.

requirements.text: Score every card transaction before the authorization decision, using the cardholder's recent activity (for example, the spending of the last hour and the last day).
Update the model as new confirmed fraud cases arrive.
For any past score, show which model version and which input values produced it.
During a seasonal peak of 15,000 transactions per second, a score comes back within 30 ms at the 99th percentile.
When the scoring service or one of its data sources fails, authorizations go on. The business accepts weaker fraud detection for up to 15 minutes, but no authorization may fail because of scoring.
An auditor asks about a score from up to 13 months ago. Within one working day the team answers with the model version, the input values and the training data that model was built from.
When the fraud loss rate rises in one segment, a retrained model can be in production within 48 hours, after it has been compared with the current model on recent transactions.
Card data must stay inside the company's PCI-certified environment: no external service may process it.
Seven people build and run the system, with no dedicated ML platform team.

points.description: The scorer runs as stateless replicas, reading cardholder-keyed online features from Redis and applying local rules if scoring is unavailable. It records each decision with its model and input snapshot, while operations manages the open-source components and scheduled jobs retrain models after labels mature. Trade-off: This provides scalable serving, fallback resilience, reproducible auditability, and controlled retraining, but matured-label scheduling makes models and features less responsive to new fraud patterns. It also requires dependable Redis and operational ownership, plus storage and handling for immutable snapshots.

A single deployment also limits independent scaling and fault isolation.

points.description: The system maintains per-cardholder state from an event-sourced transaction stream and asynchronously scores authorization requests, using a static fallback when scoring exceeds the timeout. Delayed fraud labels update the model online, while event history and model lineage support score reconstruction; the ML team operates the streaming platform. Trade-off: This provides fresh features, adaptable models, and auditable decisions with authorization-timeout resilience. It gives up operational simplicity and may reduce decision quality during scoring delays, when the static fallback is used.

options.name: Label-matured scheduled batch
values: Model updates: scheduled batch retraining after label maturation
Operations: managed open-source components owned by operations
pros: Uses confirmed labels and has a simple scheduled operating pattern.
cons: The point did not specify recent-transaction comparison or a cadence that assures the 48-hour promotion window.
options.reason: Replaced with daily challenger validation to make Q4 testable.

options.name: Custom online learning platform
values: Model updates: online updates when delayed fraud labels arrive
Operations: custom streaming platform maintained by ML team
pros: Can integrate new labels directly into a model update path.
cons: Custom platform maintenance conflicts with the small team's capacity, and online updates alone do not provide the required challenger comparison.
options.reason: Dropped because of the C2 staffing conflict and incomplete promotion gate.

adrs.title: What evidence to retain for historical score explanations
adrs.context: For any past score, the team must identify the model and inputs. Auditors may ask about scores 13 months later and need a response within one working day that also identifies the training data. The record therefore needs durable score inputs, model identity, and model training lineage.

options.name: Immutable 13-month score and training snapshots
values: Audit: immutable score log with model, input, and training dataset snapshots retained for 13 months
pros: Explicitly retains all requested evidence for the full period.
Immutable records support consistent historical reconstruction.
cons: Storage, privacy controls, and retrieval operations need capacity planning.
options.reason: Chosen to make the retention period and required audit artifacts explicit.

options.name: Append-only score, input, model, and training snapshots
values: Audit: append-only event log with versioned model and training snapshots including input values retained for 13 months
pros: Connects score inputs to model and training artifacts in an append-only history.
cons: Retention duration and response process still need operational policy.
options.reason: Chosen because it captures the full lineage while fitting the stream replay approach.

options.name: Immutable score records with dataset references
values: Audit: immutable score records with model version, input values, and training dataset references retained for 13 months
pros: Records model identity, inputs, and the training dataset reference for each score.
cons: The alternative must enforce 13-month retention and keep referenced datasets available.
options.reason: Chosen as direct score evidence with dataset lineage, with retention policy to be specified.

options.name: Model and input snapshot only
values: Audit: immutable decision log with model and input snapshot
pros: Explains which model and values produced a score.
cons: Does not identify the training data or specify a 13-month retention period.
options.reason: Insufficient for the full historical audit scenario.

options.name: Versioned model and training snapshot without explicit inputs
values: Audit: append-only event log with versioned model and training snapshots
pros: Preserves model versions and training lineage.
cons: Does not explicitly retain input values needed to reproduce a score explanation.
options.reason: Refined to include captured score inputs.
